category_title: Students with ASD and profound hearing loss exhibiting escape-motivated tantrums during academic tasks
student_description: Charlie is an 8-year-old boy with ASD and profound hearing loss whose tantrums during difficult reading are escape-motivated: he screams, pounds the table, leaves his chair, and refuses work when reading demands feel aversive. The evidence shows he needs the escape function replaced with appropriate, brief break communication while reading demands remain in place and are made more attainable through reinforcement and task-size adjustments.

criteria.criterion_name: Analysis of what makes reading escapable
criteria.rationale: Charlie’s tantrums are tied to escaping difficult reading work, so sustained improvement requires identifying whether workload, difficulty, or other task features are driving avoidance.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes ongoing analysis of the reading demands that trigger escape behavior and uses those findings to calibrate the amount or difficulty of work.

criteria.rationale: Charlie needs reading expectations increased gradually so he can contact reinforcement for successful engagement rather than being overwhelmed by full difficult assignments.
criteria.check: The long-term plan reinforces successful completion or honest attempts at progressively increasing amounts of reading work rather than expecting immediate full-task compliance.

criteria.criterion_name: Tantrums do not produce lasting escape
criteria.rationale: Because Charlie’s tantrums have been strengthened by removal of reading materials, a long-term plan must consistently prevent tantrum behavior from functioning as the route out of work.
criteria.check: The long-term plan specifies that reading demands are not removed as a consequence of tantrums and that any breaks or delays are brief, structured, and earned through appropriate communication or work engagement.
